mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 0.2% and a fall in PAYEMS below -0.1% in the same month signals labor market tightness with employment contraction, which increases uncertainty and reduces growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 0.2% AND PAYEMS < -0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST below -5% for three consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and home-related consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.5% and a decrease in CPIAUCSL below 1.5% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy with subdued inflation, which increases discount rates but does not offset cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.

regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 8% in a single month signals a surge in personal savings, which may reflect precautionary behavior and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +8% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
